title: CloVR-ITS: Automated ITS amplicon sequence analysis pipeline for fungal microbiota analysis– standard operating procedure, version 1.0
protocol: Check each read from the sequence pool for quality.
Sort sequences based on the sample-specific barcodes.
Use QIIME script split_libraries.py with parameters --min-seq-length 100, --max-seq-length 2000, --barcode-type variable_length, --max-homopolymer 8, --min-qual-score 25, and --max-ambig 0.
Generate a single set of filtered reads identified by sample meeting the quality criteria.
Cluster all non-chimeric reads from all samples into genus-level operational taxonomic units (OTUs) using UCLUST with a nucleotide sequence identity threshold of 85%.
Examine both forward and reverse complement sequences during clustering.
Reorganize genus-level OTUs created by QIIME commands.
Input the reorganized OTUs to Mothur for alpha-diversity analysis.
Use Mothur scripts read.otu, rarefaction.single, and summary.single to generate rarefaction curves and species diversity estimators for each sample.
Plot all rarefaction curves together using a custom program called Leech with color schemes related to the input mapping file.
Search non-chimeric representative sequences from 99% clusters against a custom ITSreference database using BLASTN with options "-e 1.0e-5", "-b 10", and "-m 8".
Assign each sequence to the taxonomic lineage of the best BLAST alignment covering at least 90% of the query sequence length.
Denote sequences as "Unclassified" if alignments do not meet coverage or identity thresholds for specific taxonomic levels.
Propagate hits across corresponding clusters.
Normalize taxon counts using a custom R script called skiff.
Calculate distance matrices for samples and taxonomic groups using Euclidean distance metric with skiff.
Create dendrograms of samples and taxa using complete-linkage clustering in the .pdf format.
Include R packages RColorBrewer and gplots for this task.
Form pie charts displaying proportions of sequences assigned to specific functional and taxonomic levels for up to 12 samples.
Output pie chart visualizations in .pdf format.
